title: Introduce lightweight toolchain bundles and release quiesce hook to reduce premerge cost
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: presubmit latency and toolchain image churn are major contributors to developer feedback time and CI cost on large PRs. This change splits the monolithic toolchain image into minimal language+tool bundles, wires a presubmit 'weight' selector so only relevant bundles are prepared for a change, and adds a release quiesce hook to reduce rollout churn during lockfile rotations.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces 'toolchain manifests' that declare minimal sets of binaries for each language bundle (node, python, go, rust). 2) Adds a lightweight image builder action (ci/actions/slim-toolchain) and small Dockerfiles for each language bundle. 3) Reworks presubmit workflow to select bundles based on path heuristics and an annotation on the PR (ci/presubmit/workflows/lint.yml). 4) Adds a release-side 'quiesce' hook (scripts/release/quiesce-hook.sh) that delays non-critical rollouts for up to 10 minutes during dependency rotation windows to avoid cascading redeploys. 5) Adds docs and a migration guide for infra and contributors.

Testing done: local action tests in a containerized runner, staged presubmit run on a fork with path heuristics, smoke deploy to staging with release quiesce toggled, and end-to-end CI run in the main pipeline (see CI checks).

Rollout plan: feature-gate enabled by default for main only after a 2-week dogfood period; a monitoring dashboard will track presubmit duration and image build count. If presubmit failures or significant regressions appear, the gate can be toggled off and we will revert the presubmit selector (rollback instructions documented).

Checklist: - [x] Implement slim toolkit image build action - [x] Add toolchain manifests and selector - [x] Update presubmit workflows to consult selector - [x] Add release quiesce hook and tests - [x] Add docs and migration guide - [x] Add telemetry hooks for presubmit duration and image build counts

Related: Linear ENG-2345 (presubmit-cost-profile), ENG-2401 (release-stability-improvements). Support ticket SUP-8921 requested targeted dep update windows for customers, which motivated the quiesce hook.

Notes on backward compatibility: existing monolithic images are still built by the release pipeline for a transitional period; nothing in this PR forces users to pin new images. The presubmit selector defaults to conservative behavior (build all bundles) until the two-week dogfood completes.
commits: init: add minimal toolchain manifest format and example manifests
feat(ci): add slim-toolchain action and per-language Dockerfiles
refactor(ci): presubmit workflow reads toolchain manifest and selects bundles
chore(release): add quiesce-hook.sh and wiring into release pipeline
docs: add toolchain-slimmer guide and migration steps
test: add integration smoke tests for presubmit selector and quiesce behavior
review_comments: Marco Li: Nice reduction in image size. Two comments: (1) path heuristics may miss generated code folders; add opt-in PR annotation and document it, (2) please add a flag to disable quiesce for hotfix windows.
Aisha Patel: Added PR annotation opt-in and documented fallback behavior; quiesce hook now accepts a --force flag used by release tooling for hotfixes.
Sana Kapoor: Can we add a Canary job that mirrors the current monolithic build for one week? I'd like to compare cache hit/miss behavior.
Aisha Patel: Added a lightweight canary stage to the nightly pipeline that triggers monolithic builds for one selected repo path per day (configurable).
release_notes: Introduce per-language slim toolchain bundles to reduce presubmit image build time and CI resource usage
Add presubmit selector that builds only impacted bundles by default, with an opt-out annotation
Add release quiesce hook to reduce rollout churn during dep rotation windows
Docs and migration guide for infra and contributors
